topic: VCM - miniature moving-coil linear actuator (brief-specified part)
citation: Moticont. LVCM-010-013-01 Linear Voice Coil Motor: product page and metric drawing LVCM-010-013-01M (revision field blank; undated).
task_or_setup: Manufacturer specification table and continuous-force-vs-stroke curve for a 9.5 mm OD housed moving-coil VCM
participants_or_bench: not applicable (manufacturer data; test method not published)
comparator: Other sub-15 mm VCMs (AMF-02 to AMF-05)
key_quantitative_findings: Continuous force 0.28 N; intermittent force 0.88 N at 10% duty; force constant Kf 0.29 N/A; back-EMF 0.29 V/(m/s); stroke 6.4 mm; coil clearance 0.33 mm per side; coil resistance 1.9 ohm; inductance 0.2 mH at 1 kHz; max continuous power 1.8 W; coil assembly 2.5 g; body 3.8 g; housing OD 9.5 mm x 12.7 mm, 20.7 mm overall at mid-stroke. Continuous force falls to about 0.18 N at the stroke end (read from plot). MY CALCULATION: Km = Kf/sqrt(R) = 0.29/sqrt(1.9) = 0.21 N/sqrt(W) (check: 0.28 N/sqrt(1.8 W) = 0.21); holding 0.3 N needs about 2.0 W (1.03 A); 1.6 N needs about 58 W (5.5 A, 10.5 V).
units_and_conditions: All values at 25 degC (drawing note); continuous rating presumably free air; max coil temperature and thermal resistance not published
locator: Drawing LVCM-010-013-01M: specification table (lower left) and continuous-force plot
limitations: Thermal resistance, max coil temperature and test method not published; no revision letter; force varies with stroke position.
relevance_to_design: Fits a 10-13 mm bore, but shows that direct-drive VCM force at this size is far below the 0.3-1.6 N transverse load at acceptable power.
transferability_reason: Same size class, voltage and load regime as the pen actuator; per-unit manufacturer data.
design_implication: Reject as nib actuator: even a lever giving nib Km 2.26 N/sqrt(W) (0.5 W at 1.6 N) would need a ratio of about 11:1, which is more than its +/-3.2 mm stroke allows for +/-0.5 mm at the nib (my calc).

topic: Actuator figure of merit and flexure safety factor (moving-magnet actuator + flexure)
citation: Hiemstra DB, Parmar G, Awtar S. Performance Tradeoffs Posed by Moving Magnet Actuators in Flexure-Based Nanopositioning. IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics (accepted-manuscript PDF).
task_or_setup: Lumped magnetostatic derivation of moving-magnet-actuator tradeoffs, then design, build and test of a single-axis flexure nanopositioner
participants_or_bench: Bench prototype: MMA plus double-parallelogram flexure bearing
comparator: Piezo stacks, quasi-static and ultrasonic piezomotors, voice-coil actuators (literature review in paper)
key_quantitative_findings: Actuator constant (force per sqrt(power)) is the traditional figure of merit. For traditional MMAs, force is proportional to sqrt(moving-magnet mass) x sqrt(power), which defines a 'dynamic actuator constant'. Flexure beams 0.75 x 25.4 x 80 mm give motion stiffness 3.43 N/mm and +/-5 mm stroke with a safety factor of 4 against yielding (natural frequency 25 Hz). The system achieved 10 mm range, 4 nm resolution and less than 0.5 degC temperature rise with a passive thermal-management system. Ultrasonic piezomotors reach 100-500 mm/s but under 10 N, and quasi-static and ultrasonic piezomotors have low fatigue life (cited).
units_and_conditions: As reported; macro-scale stage
locator: Abstract; Sec. II-A (actuator review); Sec. III (tradeoffs); flexure design and thermal-management sections (pp. 1-3, 8)
limitations: Macro-scale nanopositioner rather than pen scale; piezomotor statements are literature citations.
relevance_to_design: Supports ranking actuators by Km and moving mass, treating thermal management as first-order, and a flexure safety factor of about 4 on yield.
transferability_reason: The scaling laws transfer; geometry and thermal environment differ.
design_implication: Rank candidates by nib-referred Km and reflected moving mass; design flexures with safety factor 4 or more on yield (static), then check fatigue separately (see AMF-19, AMF-26).
search_query: direct URL (after WebSearch budget exhausted): https://psdl.engin.umich.edu/publications.php -> pdf/J18.pdf

topic: OIS VCM actuator stroke and driver heat (patent)
citation: Apple Inc. US10187573B2, Camera voice coil motor driver circuit with variable power supply input voltage (priority 2015-07-13).
task_or_setup: Patent description of OIS VCM driver architecture
participants_or_bench: not applicable
comparator: Fixed-supply linear VCM drivers (prior art described)
key_quantitative_findings: The OIS actuator stroke command is 'up to 200 microns'. The VCM driver 'may be any suitable linear or switch mode current driver'. The VCM driver of a smartphone 'spends the majority of its time ... driving less than 50% of its maximum output current', and driver heat at low output current is a thermal problem (the motivation for a variable supply voltage). Coil resistance and force values: not published.
units_and_conditions: Descriptive; no test conditions
locator: Detailed description (Google Patents full text)
limitations: No coil resistance, force or current values; a patent is not bench data.
relevance_to_design: Places OIS VCMs at about 0.2 mm stroke with light loads, and shows that linear current drivers waste heat.
transferability_reason: Same actuator physics and driver problem, but a much smaller stroke and load than the pen.
design_implication: Off-the-shelf OIS actuators are under-stroked for +/-0.5 mm. For a linear current driver from a 1S cell at 0.3 A into 1.9 ohm, driver loss is about 0.94 W against 0.17 W in the coil (my calc), so use PWM H-bridges or supply tracking.

topic: Flexure design guidance - allowable deflection vs yield and safety factor
citation: Awtar S. Synthesis and Analysis of Parallel Kinematic XY Flexure Mechanisms. PhD thesis, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, February 2004.
task_or_setup: Beam-flexure design limits and material selection for an XY flexure stage
participants_or_bench: Analytical; AL6061-T651 prototype discussed
key_quantitative_findings: With the maximum-shear-stress yield criterion, max allowable tip displacement is Delta/L <= (1/(3*eta)) * (Sy/E) * (L/T), where eta is a safety factor chosen for stress concentration. L/T ratios of 50 are common. Sy/E ranges from 4e-3 (AL-6061) to 1e-2 (Ti). Typical max deformation is 0.05L-0.1L, but in practice it is kept well within this when fatigue loading is considered. Beryllium copper has an excellent Sy/E but was rejected for fabricability; AL6061-T651 was chosen for low internal stress.
units_and_conditions: Static yield criterion; fatigue treated qualitatively
locator: Sec. 3, eq. (3.2) (PDF p. 56); material selection (PDF p. 158)
limitations: Static yield basis; no numeric fatigue allowable; Smith (2000) and Howell (2001) texts were not accessed.
relevance_to_design: Gives the sizing relation linking flexure length and thickness to the +/-0.5 mm stroke at a chosen stress.
transferability_reason: Beam mechanics are scale-independent.
design_implication: Size flexure beams on the fatigue allowable (about 150 MPa for C17200 TH04) in place of Sy/eta. MY CALC example: a fixed-guided beam has sigma = 3*E*T*delta/L^2, so L >= sqrt(3*T*delta/alpha) with alpha = sigma/E = 150/127600 = 1.18e-3. For T = 0.1 mm and delta = 0.5 mm, L >= 11.3 mm; for T = 0.05 mm, L >= 8.0 mm.

topic: Touch-temperature limits - medical electrical equipment (IEC 60601-1)
citation: IEC 60601-1:2005 Medical electrical equipment - Part 1: General requirements for basic safety and essential performance, identical adoption IS 13450 (Part 1):2008, Bureau of Indian Standards (Public.Resource.Org copy).
participants_or_bench: not applicable (consensus limits for healthy adult skin)
key_quantitative_findings: Table 23 (parts likely to be touched), for t <1 s / 1-10 s / 10 s-1 min / >=1 min: metal and liquids 74 / 56 / 51 / 48 degC; glass, porcelain 80 / 66 / 56 / 48; moulded material, plastic, rubber, wood 86 / 71 / 60 / 48. Table 24 (applied parts in contact with patient): t <1 min 51 (metal) / 56 (glass) / 60 (plastic) degC; 1-10 min 48 for all; >=10 min 43 for all. Clause 11.1.2.2: if an applied part not intended to supply heat exceeds 41 degC, its max temperature must be disclosed in the instructions for use and clinical effects assessed; at or below 41 degC no justification is needed. Limits apply to healthy adult skin and less than 10% of body surface. Table 22: insulation class A 105, E 120, B 130, F 155, H 180 degC.
units_and_conditions: Surface temperatures; worst-case ambient per technical description
locator: Clause 11.1, Tables 22-24, pp. 139-140 (PDF p. 158)
limitations: 2005 edition without amendments A1:2012 / A2:2020 (verify current text). A writing pen is ME equipment only if marketed as a medical device; that is plausible for a tremor aid.
relevance_to_design: Continuously held grip (>=10 min) is limited to 43 degC, and 41 degC triggers disclosure.
transferability_reason: Directly applicable if regulated as medical; conservative otherwise.
design_implication: Provisional limit: grip and any surface held continuously <=43 degC absolute at max rated ambient; design target <=41 degC. Briefly touched metal <=48 degC.

topic: Touch-temperature limits - hazard-based ICT safety (precursor of IEC 62368-1)
citation: Ecma International. ECMA-287 Safety of electronic equipment, 2nd edition, December 2002.
participants_or_bench: not applicable
key_quantitative_findings: Table 5.2: continuously held, all materials: 43 degC. Handles, knobs, grips held or touched for short periods only: metallic 55 degC, non-metallic 65 degC. External surfaces that may be touched: metallic 65 degC, non-metallic 85 degC. Notes: continuous holding assumed below 8 h with less than 10% of skin surface, limit derived from EN 563; short-period holding below 10 s; 'may be touched' below 1 s; metal covered by at least 0.3 mm of plastic may use the non-metallic limit. If limits are exceeded for functional reasons or above 40 degC ambient a warning is required, but hand-held equipment with a non-metallic surface need not carry the warning label.
units_and_conditions: Surface temperatures under normal operating conditions (Annex B.5)
locator: Clause 5.1.1, Table 5.2, p. 63 (PDF p. 79)
limitations: Superseded hazard-based precursor; IEC 62368-1 Table 38 (TS1/TS2 by duration) was not accessed, so its values must be confirmed. IEC 62471 (photobiological) is not relevant.
relevance_to_design: Gives the same 43 degC continuous-hold limit as IEC 60601-1.
transferability_reason: Same hazard basis as current ICT/AV safety standard.
design_implication: Adopt 43 degC continuous-hold as the provisional TS1-equivalent limit for the barrel. A plastic sleeve of 0.3 mm or more over metal allows the non-metallic class for brief contact.

Integrated current mirror (IPROPI) with gain select: 225 uA/A (0.35-2 A), 1125 uA/A (60-350 mA), 5560 uA/A (10-60 mA). Total error +/-5% (1 A and 250 mA ranges) and +/-6.5% (50 mA range).
